walkthrough.title: Where is that car's odometer right now?
walkthrough.subtitle: Divinecodes · Project 2 · SIXT Hackathon
points: Estimate current mileage
Forecast future mileage
Find reports worth reviewing
walkthrough.narration: This is team Divinecodes, presenting Project Two: mileage forecasting and erroneous mileage detection. We built a local pipeline and an interactive demonstration to estimate a rental car's current mileage, forecast future mileage, and identify reports that deserve a closer look.

walkthrough.title: The problem: readings arrive late
walkthrough.subtitle: Why this matters to SIXT
points: A car can stay with a customer for weeks
The recorded odometer becomes outdated
Valuation and defleet decisions still need an estimate
walkthrough.narration: During a long rental, the latest recorded odometer may be weeks out of date. SIXT still needs to value the car and decide when to remove it from the rental fleet. A nowcast estimates mileage today. A forecast estimates mileage on a future date. Suspicious reading detection helps analysts find possible entry mistakes or unusual usage.

walkthrough.title: We connected the supplied Parquet data
walkthrough.subtitle: Development evidence and separate inference targets
points: Use development data for evaluation
Keep masked targets separate from tuning
Empty organizer prediction columns are not model features
walkthrough.narration: The development sample contains nearly two point seven million status rows across twenty seven thousand, six hundred and thirty vehicles. We added Parquet support and streaming fleet loading. The separate inference file has one hundred and sixty three thousand, forty seven missing mileage targets. We keep those targets separate from model tuning and do not use the empty organizer prediction or error columns as features.

walkthrough.title: The key insight: two different clocks
walkthrough.subtitle: Measurement date is different from availability date
points: An OnRent value may be an older handover reading
Retiming a value must not make it available earlier
Rental metadata and changing categories obey the same boundary
The pattern is not universal: verify the source semantics
walkthrough.narration: Our main insight is that the date a mileage value belongs to can differ from the date the system first knows it. Some On Rent rows contain older handover mileage. We retime those values, but never reveal them before their row was recorded. We apply the same availability boundary to rental metadata and changing vehicle categories. The fleet pattern is not universal, so we document the assumption rather than treating every row as certain truth.

walkthrough.title: Compare methods, then evaluate honestly
walkthrough.subtitle: Choose before looking at held-out outcomes
points: Last-reading and average-rate baselines
Rental-aware rates, recent rates, a blend and a robust candidate
Separate model selection from interval calibration
Test on later periods and held-out vehicles
walkthrough.narration: We compared the last recorded reading, an average daily rate, rental aware models, a recent usage variant, a blend, and a robust rate candidate. Earlier validation chooses the model separately for each task. A different later period calibrates the prediction ranges. Final evaluation uses later readings on held out vehicles. Future field mutation tests check that changing future rows cannot change earlier predictions.

walkthrough.title: Live walkthrough: estimate the current mileage
walkthrough.subtitle: All dashboard vehicles and readings are synthetic
points: Choose a vehicle
Compare last reading with the current estimate
Read the age and uncertainty range
walkthrough.narration: Here is the working dashboard. Every vehicle in this demonstration is made up. Select a car on the left. The first card shows its last recorded mileage and the age of that reading. The orange card shows the model's current estimate and a prediction range. The timeline connects the known history to the estimate, making the gap visible instead of hiding the uncertainty.

walkthrough.title: Change the planning horizon
walkthrough.subtitle: Precomputed Python model outputs · not an invented browser calculation
points: Switch between 7, 30, 60 and 90 days
Inspect the future estimate and its range
Export the selected result to CSV
walkthrough.narration: Next, change the forecast horizon from thirty days to ninety days. The future estimate and its range update using outputs precomputed by the Python models. Longer horizons can require much wider ranges. The page also supports searching, filtering, and exporting the selected estimate as a CSV. The demo works offline and needs no API key.

walkthrough.title: Make suspicious reports explainable
walkthrough.subtitle: A review signal is not proof of fraud
points: An invented mileage spike is flagged
Each signal includes a date, reason and context
Transfers, delayed data and unusual usage can also trigger flags
walkthrough.narration: The review queue includes an intentionally invented mileage spike. Each signal shows the report date, the reading, and a reason for investigation. Our rules cover isolated spikes or dips, decreases, implausible rates, movement without recorded rentals, unchanged readings during rental days, and model residual outliers. A flag is a request for review. It is not proof of fraud, and real precision still requires domain expert labels.

walkthrough.title: Measured results on held-out data
walkthrough.subtitle: Average absolute error in kilometres · lower is better
walkthrough.narration: On held out development readings, current mileage error falls from five hundred and sixty one kilometres for the last reading baseline to four hundred and fifteen. Forecast error falls from seven thousand, three hundred and seventy six kilometres to two thousand, seven hundred and thirty four. Those are reductions of twenty six percent and sixty two point nine percent. The selected models also beat the stronger average rate baseline. These are fleet evaluation results, separate from the synthetic dashboard.

walkthrough.title: Measure detection, report its limits
walkthrough.subtitle: Known injected mistakes provide a controlled check
points: Episode recall can credit a rollback neighbour
Untouched flags can include pre-existing problems
Do not turn review signals into accusations
walkthrough.narration: In a controlled development benchmark, the detector caught four hundred and fifty one of four hundred and seventy nine injected mistakes: ninety four point two percent episode recall. Exact corrupted reading recall was ninety three point nine percent. Episode recall can also credit the reading immediately before a rollback. This does not establish real world precision. Untouched readings may already contain errors, and some flags may reflect missing or stale operational data.

walkthrough.title: The missing-mileage output is complete
walkthrough.subtitle: Original table preserved · unsupported certainty avoided
points: Future targets use the forecast recipe
No own history: clearly mark the cohort fallback
Leave sixt_error unchanged when truth is missing
walkthrough.narration: We filled all one hundred and sixty three thousand, forty seven missing mileage targets and preserved the original table. Most use the vehicle's own earlier history with a range. Three thousand, seven hundred and forty five have no usable own history, so they receive an explicitly flagged fleet cohort fallback. Those fallbacks have no calibrated range and need review. The error column stays unchanged because the masked ground truth is unavailable.

walkthrough.title: A reproducible project, ready for review
walkthrough.subtitle: Code · evaluation evidence · visual demo · presentation
points: 31 automated tests pass
Public example runs without organizer data
Self-contained offline dashboard and five-slide PDF
Next: expert labels, long-term validation and a shadow-mode pilot
walkthrough.narration: The project includes reproducible commands, measured aggregate evidence, thirty one passing tests, an offline dashboard, and a five slide presentation. A clean source copy runs the public example without organizer data. The next step is a shadow mode pilot: confirm measurement semantics, label representative flags, and validate long term rentals and range coverage. We demonstrate a working decision aid, not proven fraud detection, guaranteed savings, or production readiness.
